doc: F1 and F2 (distances to the nearest and second-nearest feature point, in cell units, one jittered point per unit cell, the 27 neighbor cells searched) at 1500 random float32 points in [-4, 4]^3 (cells of both signs: a negative cell index is wrapped by & 1023). float32 outputs, F1 <= F2, F1 < 1.08 and F2 < 1.2 over these points. Measured against the float64 evaluation of the same inputs: 1.3e-7 at most; the default tolerance (1e-5 rel, 1e-6 abs) is 10x that. The values are continuous in the point (min of distances), so there is no hard threshold even where the nearest cell changes. The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
